problems.title: Split people into three named groups
problems.question: In how many ways can 21 people be split equally into named groups A,B,C?
problems.idea: Choose the members of one group at a time.
formulas: Choose k of n without ordering: C(n,k)=n!/[k!(n-k)!].
steps: Choose 7 of 21 people for A: C(21,7) choices.
Choose 7 of the remaining 14 for B: C(14,7) choices.
The last 7 form C automatically. The group names are distinct, so no division by 3! is needed.

problems.title: Count repeated digits by complement
problems.question: How many three-digit integers have at least two equal digits?
problems.idea: Subtract numbers with all digits distinct from all three-digit integers.
steps: There are 900 three-digit integers from 100 to 999.
For all distinct digits, there are 9 choices for the first, 9 for the second including zero, and 8 for the third.

problems.title: Height of a square-pyramid frustum
problems.question: A regular square-pyramid frustum has base sides 2 and 6 and apothem 5. Find its height.
problems.idea: The slant height’s horizontal projection is half the difference of the base sides.

problems.title: Choose a director and three deputies
problems.question: Choose a director and three deputies from seven candidates. How many choices are possible?
problems.idea: The director’s role is distinct; the three deputies form an unordered group.
steps: From the remaining 6, choose any 3 deputies: C(6,3)=20.
problems.note: This treats the three deputy roles as indistinguishable. If the posts were separately named, the count would be 7·6·5·4=840; the question does not name separate posts.

problems.title: Recognize a fifth-power binomial
problems.question: Factor 80a⁴b+32a⁵+80a³b²+40a²b³+10ab⁴+b⁵.
problems.idea: Compare the coefficients with the binomial expansion.
steps: They match all the displayed terms, after reordering.

problems.title: Combine combinations and ordered arrangements
problems.question: Evaluate [C(10,2)+C(10,8)]/A(5,3).
problems.idea: Use complement symmetry for combinations.

problems.title: Area bounded by three linear inequalities
problems.question: Find the area defined by y≥-1,x≥1,y≤-0.75x+3.
problems.idea: The boundary lines form a right triangle.
steps: At x=1, the upper boundary has y=9/4, so the vertical leg is 13/4.
At y=-1, the upper boundary gives x=16/3, so the horizontal leg is 13/3.

problems.title: Probability of a solvable sine-cosine equation
problems.question: a is uniformly chosen from [-20,20]. Find the probability that 5sinx+12cosx=a has a real solution.
problems.idea: The left side has amplitude 13.
formulas: Acosx+Bsinx ranges over [-√(A²+B²),√(A²+B²)]; uniform probability=interval-length ratio.
steps: Its length is 26; the sampling interval has length 40.

problems.title: At least one chosen coin face in five tosses
problems.question: A fair coin is tossed independently five times. Find the chance of getting the specified face at least once.
problems.idea: Subtract the probability of never seeing it.
steps: Missing that face on all five tosses has probability (1/2)⁵=1/32.

problems.title: Lateral areas after a half-height cut
problems.question: A base-parallel plane through a pyramid’s height midpoint splits it into a small pyramid and a frustum. Find the ratio of their lateral areas.
problems.idea: The small pyramid has half the original linear scale.
formulas: Similar surface areas scale as the square of the linear factor.
steps: The small lateral area is (1/2)²=1/4 of the original.
The frustum lateral area is the remaining 3/4.
problems.note: The value 1/3 appears twice among the printed choices, so both identical choices represent the same correct ratio.

problems.title: Internal dihedral angle versus acute plane angle
problems.question: All edges of a regular square pyramid are equal. Find the cosine of the angle between adjacent lateral faces.
problems.idea: Compute the outward-normal angle, then take its supplement for the internal dihedral angle.
formulas: Internal dihedral angle=supplement of outward-normal angle; cos(π-θ)=-cosθ.
steps: Two adjacent outward face normals can be chosen as (0,-h,a/2) and (h,0,a/2), where h=a/√2.
Their dot product is a²/4 and each squared norm is h²+a²/4=3a²/4, giving outward-normal cosine 1/3.
The interior dihedral angle therefore has cosine -1/3.
problems.answer: Internal dihedral cosine: -1/3. Acute angle between the supporting planes: cosine +1/3.
problems.note: Both +1/3 and -1/3 are listed. They refer to different angle conventions; the angle inside the pyramid is the obtuse dihedral angle.

problems.title: Frustum lateral area from diagonals and an inclination
problems.question: A regular square-pyramid frustum has base diagonals 2 and 6 and a 60° base dihedral angle. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Convert diagonals to sides, then find the face altitude from its horizontal projection.
formulas: Square side=diagonal/√2; slant height=apothem difference/cos60°; lateral area=(perimeter sum)·slant height/2.
steps: The base sides are √2 and 3√2, so the horizontal apothem difference is √2.

problems.title: Distance from a point above a right triangle to a leg
problems.question: ABC is right-angled at B. AD is perpendicular to the triangle plane, AD=AC=6 and cosA=2/3. Find the distance from D to BC.
problems.idea: AB is perpendicular to BC, and AD is perpendicular to the whole base plane.
steps: DB is perpendicular to BC because both its components BA and AD are perpendicular to BC.

problems.title: Middle term of a tenth-power expansion
problems.question: Find the middle term of $(x^{-1/5}+x^{1/3})^{10}$.
problems.idea: There are eleven terms, so use the sixth term with k=5.
steps: Thus the middle term is 252x^(2/3), on the original domain x≠0.

problems.title: Angle between a cube face diagonal and a diagonal plane
problems.question: In cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁, find the cosine of the angle between DC₁ and plane BB₁D₁D.
problems.idea: Use a direction vector and a plane normal.
steps: The direction DC₁ is (1,0,1); the plane is x+y=1 with normal (1,1,0).
The acute line-plane angle has cosine √3/2.

problems.title: Possible base angle of a regular pentagonal pyramid face
problems.question: Which listed value can be a lateral face’s base angle in a regular pentagonal pyramid: 120°,39°,65°,50°,90°,47°?
problems.idea: The nonzero pyramid height makes this angle greater than its flat limiting value.
steps: A nondegenerate pyramid has lateral edge greater than R.
The isosceles lateral triangle also requires β<90°.

problems.title: Face, edge and vertex counts of a frustum
problems.question: Which listed number can be the sum of a pyramid frustum’s vertices, edges and faces: 101,102,103,104,105,106?
problems.idea: A frustum over an n-gon has the same counts as an n-gonal prism.
steps: The total must leave remainder 2 modulo 6.

problems.title: Total square-prism area from a diagonal inclination
problems.question: A regular square prism has base side √3 cm. Its space diagonal makes 30° with a lateral-face plane. Find the total surface area.
problems.idea: The perpendicular component of the diagonal to that face is one base side.

problems.title: Equal lateral edges force a cyclic base
problems.question: If every lateral edge of a pyramid is equal, which listed base shape is impossible?
problems.idea: The apex projection must be equally far from every base vertex.
formulas: A set of planar vertices equally far from one point lies on a circle.
steps: The base must be cyclic. Rectangles, all triangles, and isosceles trapezoids are cyclic.
A genuine right trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides is not cyclic: a cyclic trapezoid must be isosceles.
A rhombus is cyclic only when it is a square. A square is allowed if included under “rhombus.”
problems.answer: A genuine right trapezoid; a nonsquare rhombus is also impossible.
problems.note: The rhombus choice depends on whether squares are included in that label. Equal lateral edges allow the square case but exclude every nonsquare rhombus.

problems.title: Surface area under a ten-percent length reduction
problems.question: All edges of a regular hexagonal pyramid are reduced by 10%. By what percent does its lateral area decrease?
problems.idea: This is a uniform similarity scale.
steps: The new area is 0.9²=0.81 of the old area.

problems.title: Compare signed binomial terms
problems.question: For which x is the fifth term of (2x-3)⁹ greater than both neighbouring terms?
problems.idea: Compare the actual signed fourth, fifth and sixth terms.
steps: The relevant terms are T₄=-145152x⁶, T₅=326592x⁵, T₆=-489888x⁴.
T₅>T₄ is equivalent to x⁵(x+9/4)>0, giving x< -9/4 or x>0.
T₅>T₆ requires x⁴(x+3/2)>0, giving x> -3/2 and x≠0.
Their intersection is x>0. At zero all three terms are equal, so it is excluded.

problems.title: Solve a combination identity
problems.question: Find n if C(n+4,n+1)+C(n+3,n)=13(n+2)(n+3)/6.
problems.idea: Convert both combinations to choosing three.
steps: For the allowed nonnegative integer n, cancel (n+2)(n+3)/6.

problems.title: At least two known questions on a ticket
problems.question: A pupil knows 6 of 10 questions. A ticket contains 3 distinct questions chosen uniformly. Find the probability of knowing at least 2.
problems.idea: Separate the cases of exactly two and exactly three known questions.

problems.title: Four students placed in distinct classrooms
problems.question: Four students are assigned independently and uniformly to seven classrooms. Find the chance that all four receive different classrooms.
problems.idea: Count ordered classroom assignments.

problems.title: Identify a term in a binomial expansion
problems.question: Which listed term occurs in (x+2)⁸?
problems.idea: Use the coefficient formula for each power.
formulas: The term with x⁸⁻ᵏ is C(8,k)2ᵏx⁸⁻ᵏ.
